explain.say: Here is a strange question: where does east begin? Lines of longitude run from pole to pole, but someone had to choose which one is zero. Look at the board. This is the story of how the world picked a line through a park in Greenwich, London.

explain.say: Long ago, sailors could find their latitude from the sun, but not their longitude, which means how far east or west they were. Ships got lost and wrecked. So in 1714 Britain offered a huge prize, 20,000 pounds, for an answer. What would you have invented?

explain.say: A clockmaker called John Harrison had the answer: a clock that keeps perfect time at sea. Compare it with noon where you are, and every hour of difference means 15 degrees of longitude. Look at 1761: his H4 clock passed its test on a voyage to Jamaica.

explain.say: But countries still used different zero lines, which was confusing. In 1884, 25 nations met in Washington and voted for Greenwich, mostly because ships already used sea charts based on it. France abstained and kept its Paris line until 1911. Can you see why one shared line helps everyone?

faq.a: Longitude tells you how far east or west a place is from the Prime Meridian, in degrees from 0 to 180. Lines of longitude run from the North Pole to the South Pole.

faq.q: Why was longitude so hard to find at sea?
faq.a: To know your longitude you must compare your local time with the time at a fixed place, and old clocks could not keep good time on rolling ships. Without it, sailors could not tell how far east or west they had gone.

John Harrison was an English carpenter and clockmaker who built very accurate sea clocks called marine chronometers. His fourth clock, H4, kept time well enough on a voyage to Jamaica to find longitude.

faq.q: Why was Greenwich chosen as the Prime Meridian?
faq.a: At the 1884 International Meridian Conference most nations voted for Greenwich, mainly because most of the world’s shipping already used sea charts based on it. One country voted against, and France and Brazil abstained.

Why is the Prime Meridian in Greenwich?

faq.q: Is the Prime Meridian line in Greenwich exact?
faq.a: The famous brass line marks the meridian chosen in 1884. Modern satellite systems use a reference meridian about 102 metres to the east, because of the way they measure the shape of the Earth.
asks: Why is the GPS zero line in a different place?

facts: The Royal Observatory in Greenwich was founded in 1675.
The Longitude Act of 1714 offered up to £20,000 for a practical way to find longitude at sea.
The International Meridian Conference of 1884 in Washington, D.C. chose Greenwich as the Prime Meridian.

quiz.say: What did sailors need in order to find their longitude at sea?
quiz.show: To find longitude at sea, sailors needed…
quiz.why: Comparing local noon with the time on an accurate clock tells you how far east or west you are.

wrong.1: Sails move the ship but cannot tell you where you are.
wrong.2: A lamp helps you see, but longitude needs accurate time.

quiz.say: In which year did nations vote for Greenwich as 0 degrees longitude?
quiz.show: Greenwich was chosen as the Prime Meridian in…
quiz.why: The International Meridian Conference voted for Greenwich in 1884.

wrong.1: 1714 is when Britain offered the longitude prize.
wrong.2: 1969 is the year of the first Moon landing, long after the vote.
